subject: Latency spike after model canary (v2.1) — RampWave escalation
messages:
From: Nadia Park <nadia.park@rampwave.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-support@rampwave.ai, victor.cheng@orchid.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

Team —

We started seeing a major uplift in user-facing latency around 07:45 PDT after your scheduled canary (v2.1) landed. P95 jumped from ~180ms to 1.2s and p99 from ~340ms to ~2.6s across our production traffic. Error rate is slightly elevated (~0.4% -> 1.1%) and throughput looks OK. This is impacting our logged-in users (search/autocomplete flows).

We rolled back on our side where possible but the hosted API calls still return the slower tail. Please advise immediate rollback plan and ETA — our execs are asking for visibility. Attaching a quick CSV with traces.

-Nadia
RampWave — SRE
attachments: rampwave_latency_snapshot_20280927.csv
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Park <nadia.park@rampwave.ai>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, victor.cheng@orchid.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

Nadia —

Thank you for the heads up and the CSV. We see the same signal in our traces and are treating this as high priority. Immediate steps:

- I have spun up an incident channel and notified SRE/Eng (sean + ben on this thread).
- Please hold any further rollback attempts; we may need to coordinate a platform-side rollback to avoid inconsistent routes.
- Can you share the exact request IDs for any failed calls? If you can paste 2-3 trace IDs that show the 2.6s tails that will help.

We will: (1) confirm whether the v2.1 canary was routed to your traffic, (2) evaluate a roll-forward patch vs rollback, (3) propose mitigation (route to v2.0 / rate-limit canary). Expect a status update in 30 minutes. Apologize for the disruption.

—Tessa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

On Thu, Sep 27, 2028 at 08:28 AM Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Nadia —
> 
> Thank you for the heads up...

Quick summary from SRE telemetry:
- Canary v2.1 introduced a new attention-kernel fallback for long-context sequences (experimental perf path).
- We see elevated KV-cache misses and increased GPU memcpy time on the serving tier handling affected routes.
- The increased latency aligns strongly with requests that exceed ~1.2k tokens and a particular model variant flag enabled in canary-config-v2.1.yaml.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Global rollback of v2.1 to v2.0 (fastest, ~6-9 min to complete with safe draining).
2) Route RampWave traffic to v2.0 only (per-account routing, immediate but manual).
3) Hotfix to disable experimental kernel path in v2.1 (requires a small rollout and verification, ~20-30m).

I'm starting a rollback job but will hold if leadership wants patch-first. I attached kvcache-eviction-logs.txt and the canary config for reference.

—Sean
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: kvcache-eviction-logs.txt, canary-config-v2.1.yaml
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

Team —

Thanks Sean. Quick read of the eviction traces suggests the experimental kernel is thrashing the KV cache on large-batch sequences; the resulting memcpy and kernel fallbacks create the long tail. Given customer impact, my recommendation is:

- Execute option (1) global rollback to v2.0 now to re-stabilize p95/p99.
- After rollback completes, open a focused infra task to disable the experimental attention fallback and run a canary with a narrower token distribution (no >1k token flows).
- Communicate ETA to customer during rollback and confirm monitoring.

I'll own the rollback; Sean, kick the job and confirm when drain windows are scheduled. Tessa, please update the customer and let Execs know we're rolling back; loop me in the customer call if they request one.

—Ben
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Park <nadia.park@rampwave.ai>
Cc: victor.cheng@orchid.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

Nadia —

We are initiating a platform rollback of canary v2.1 to v2.0 now. Ben is leading the operation and Sean is executing the rollback with assured drain. Expected stabilization window: 8–12 minutes after rollback completes; I will post updates in the incident channel and on this thread.

Next steps for transparency:
- We will share a short postmortem within 48 hours with root cause and mitigation plan.
- If RampWave wants a call with Ben and our SREs, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge in the next hour.

We deeply regret the disruption — thank you for flagging this quickly.

—Tessa
From: Nadia Park <nadia.park@rampwave.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-support@rampwave.ai, victor.cheng@orchid.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 latency spike after model update (RampWave prod)

Tessa / Ben / Sean —

Thank you for the rapid response and the rollback. Latency returned to normal for the last two hours (p95 ~165ms, p99 ~320ms). We appreciate the proposed postmortem and would like to join the follow-up call.

Please share the JIRA and a proposed time for the bridge.

-Nadia
RampWave SRE
